text:
kevin: hitting a weird auth race when I run `redwoodctl login --headless --token-file=/tmp/rw.token` in my dev container. sometimes it works, other times I end up with 3 browser tabs and a corrupted token file. anyone seen headless/token-file conflicts?

marta: hmm: what does "corrupted" mean for the token file? can you paste the failure?

kevin: paste: 
```
> redwoodctl login --headless --token-file=/tmp/rw.token --profile=kevin-dev
device code: open https://redwood.auth and enter CODE-XYZ
login complete
warning: failed to write token: write /tmp/rw.token: file truncated
error: auth state invalid: parse error
```

ryan: that "file truncated" smells like two concurrent login attempts racing to write the same token-file. The CLI writes atomically by writing a temp then renaming; if both processes do that against the same path you can still hit transient truncation on some filesystems or with aggressive container IO.

marta: are you running any tooling that auto-retries login? CI containers sometimes have entrypoint logic that calls login repeatedly on failure. Also some exec wrappers re-run on non-zero exit which can trigger a retry storm.

kevin: not intentionally. I do have a nodemon-like watcher in the devcontainer that runs `make dev` which calls `redwoodctl localserve` and if it sees 401 it calls `redwoodctl login --headless` to recover. So yeah, could be retry loop.

ryan: suggested quick fixes: 1) add a file lock around token-file writes in your wrapper (flock) 2) use unique token files per process: `--token-file=/tmp/rw.token.$PID` and then symlink after success 3) better: prefer `redwoodctl login --profile=kevin-dev --headless` with `redwoodctl config set profile.kevin-dev.store=true` instead of multiple processes writing the same token file.

marta: plus a CLI improvement: we should make headless login detect an existing token-file being written and wait/dedupe instead of clobbering. Also the error message should mention concurrent writers and suggest a flock/unique-file workaround.

kevin: workaround I used: `while ! redwoodctl login --headless --token-file=/tmp/rw.token; do sleep 1; done` but that still opened multiple browser tabs when the watcher raced triggers. I switched to `--token-file=/tmp/rw.token.$(date +%s%N)` and then `mv` the file into place once login succeeds. ugly but works.

ryan: filed an issue to serialize headless/token-file writes and to retry on EINVAL/truncate: we'll try to write temp file next to target and use rename-in-same-dir to avoid cross-device problems and add an exclusive lock. Also add clear guidance in the quickstart about CI and concurrent watchers.

devex-bot: Created ticket DX-5588: "redwoodctl: dedupe/lock headless token-file writes; improve error message for concurrent headless login; docs for CI and watcher loops" and linked to CLI backlog. :memo:

kevin: thanks, leaving the workaround here in case someone else has a watcher that auto-retries and spawns spurious SSO flows. saved my sanity. :coffee:
